title: In/Spectre
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: As a child, Kotoko Iwanaga was taken by yokai, lost an eye and a leg, and became their 'Goddess of Wisdom', settling spirit-world disputes. Years later she sets her heart on Kuro, a college student whose own bond with yokai makes him both useful and troubled, and the pair deal with a deadly urban legend, 'Steel Idol', while his ex-girlfriend Saki, now a police officer, is drawn in (Kodansha blurb; ANN review of volume 1).
life_message: Order between the human and spirit worlds is kept by wit and persuasion, and an unusual partnership can be built on frankness.

content.note: An urban legend 'harming people' and action scenes (ANN); MU Violence, Murder/s, Regeneration.
Yokai, ghosts and a monstrous urban legend (AniList Horror genre, Youkai; ANN).
Kotoko openly tries to seduce Kuro; cheeky innuendo (ANN); AniList Age Gap.
Kotoko's lost eye and leg handled matter-of-factly (MU Amputee/s, Prosthesis).

dominant: Folklore spirits as part of the world; pragmatic problem-solving; romantic comedy

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Disputes are settled by Kotoko's judgment and reasoning, not personal duels (Kodansha blurb).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Kotoko's role is to keep order among renegade yokai (Kodansha blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Partners and police cooperate to protect the public (ANN; MU Police).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Yokai defer to Kotoko as goddess, yet she treats Kuro as an equal partner.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Japanese folklore spirits handled through logic and investigation (MU Japanese Folklore, Investigation).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Safety from the urban legend balanced with comic romance (ANN).

folkways.japan: Yokai, kappa and urban legends come from Japanese folk belief, where such spirits are familiar rather than demonic.

delivery.evidence: ANN describes a cheeky comedy with a thin mystery; no lecturing noted (to verify).

personified.ideology: Order between spirits and humans kept by wit

delivery.note: Its ideas about order and plausible explanations come through Kotoko's problem-solving rather than speeches (to verify in later arcs).

winners_losers: Kotoko and Kuro restore order and the harmful urban legend is defeated; the spirit world is shown as a neighbor to manage, not an enemy.
